analysis:
The PR modifies only docs/provider/cli-reference.md, so no executable code changed. The supplied units are base lines 2117-2367 and 2368-end (unchanged by the PR per the changed-range map, which lists base changes only through line 1147) and head lines 1-385. Within the visible head text, the only changed line is the 'Last updated' date at line 3. The remaining documented behavior I read is unchanged context: the environment passthrough list, App Attest worker opt-in (DARKBLOOM_APP_ATTEST_WORKER_QUALIFICATION, exact '1' only), SSD prefix-cache controls (T-041), the logout and switch descriptions, and the fan helper paths. None of it introduces new attack surface or contradicts the retained threat entries.

The substantive edits sit in the Darkbloom Sandbox section (base ~1035-1147, head ~1035-1186): the `setup --linux-slots/--macos-slots` row and the rewritten 'Setup' step 1 check. These touch TB-013, A-019 and T-061 (installer download and run as the Mac owner), and TB-012 (add-on hold). The patch excerpt is truncated and those head lines were not supplied, so I could not verify whether the doc changes alter the stated trust properties. Examples to check: the `--server` https-only restriction, the sudo refusal, the installer verification description, and the claim that chosen slot counts are taken as-is, which bypasses the resource estimate. These are documentation claims whose accuracy against the code was not checked. The next pass should read the head sandbox section and compare it with the TB-013/T-061 contract, including that the removal of core/memory/disk checks from the preflight does not weaken the described admission or refusal behavior.
